title: OTLP outage-resiliency proxy with rate-aware routing and sink fallback
text:
OTLP outage-resiliency proxy with rate-aware routing and sink fallback

description:
Build an OTLP edge proxy that improves tracing ingestion availability during downstream outages by using rate-aware routing, adaptive local buffering, and deterministic sink failover. The proxy should preserve span ordering signals where possible, surface backpressure to clients via OTLP status and headers, and provide per-tenant routing policies with configurable SLAs. This ticket covers design, a prototype sidecar implementation, and an initial canary rollout plan.

acceptance_criteria:
Edge proxy routes OTLP/gRPC ingest to primary and secondary sinks based on configured weights and real-time health checks
When a primary sink reports increased error rate or latency, proxy reduces traffic to it within 30s using rate-aware algorithm and shifts to secondary sinks without loss of accepted spans
Proxy exposes metrics for dropped spans, queued bytes, and route decisions; dashboards created in Grafana and linked in docs
End-to-end integration test demonstrating failover from Tempo to S3-archival fallback with preserved tenant metadata
Security review completed for mTLS credential rotation and tenant credential handling

steps:
Draft design doc detailing routing algorithm, health checks, and queue sizing (p0)
Prototype Go-based OTLP proxy with pluggable sink drivers (tempo, jaeger, s3 archive)
Add rate-aware decision engine that uses EWMA of sink latency+error to adjust weights
Implement per-tenant token mapping and optional tenant-level rate limits
Add metrics (prometheus) and tracing for the proxy itself; wire up dashboards
Run chaos tests to simulate backend flaps and validate no silent span loss beyond configured window
Canary rollout to one region and documented rollback/playbook

comments:
2026-03-02 - Aisha Nkomo: Kickoff with infra, product, and observability leads. Agreed on EWMA-based rate adjustment and max-queue-bytes per tenant. Need security signoff for credential handling.
2026-03-04 - Liam Chen: Prototype created (branch: eng/otlp-proxy-rateaware). Early perf numbers show additional 5-8ms p99 for successful paths, queueing behaves as expected under synthetic spike.
2026-03-06 - Design review notes: PM requests that tenant-level SLA policy be expressive (min-throughput, max-latency); Design to include policy syntax examples. Design doc updated: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OtLPProxyDesign
2026-03-08 - Security review kickoff: flagged credential caching TTL and rotation; recommended using KMS-backed ephemeral certs. Security item added to release checklist.
2026-03-10 - QA: Added e2e test case that replays a trace stream while flipping tempo endpoint to 500s and asserts >=99.5% ingestion to fallback destination during window

rollback_plan:
If proxy causes dropped spans or SLO regression in canary: revert traffic to previous ingress, disable adaptive routing, and collect debug bundles. Postmortem within 72 hours.

notes:
This work complements existing trace-broker efforts but focuses on rapid edge-level mitigation for downstream outages and tenant-specific throttles. Explore using existing span-enricher hooks for synthetic heartbeat spans during long outages to aid debugging.
